newsitem.title: USA: Compaq expects to outpace industry growth.
newsitem.headline: Compaq expects to outpace industry growth.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp Chief Financial Officer Earl Mason on Wednesday said the computer maker expects to outpace estimates of 15 percent to 20 percent personal computer sales growth in the industry this year.
"We believe we will grow ahead of that," Mason said, declining to disclose sales growth projections of the Houston-based company.

Record fourth quarter sales and improved asset management during the year boosted Compaq's cash on hand to $4 billion, which will be used to bankroll internal growth and possible acquisitions, Mason told Reuters.

"What we are going to do is use the cash to grow the business," Mason said. The company will invest in "organic" growth by expanding its sales network, and it routinely mulls possible acquisitions, he said.
Compaq plans to meet with analysts Friday to discuss new asset management plans for the company, raising the bar on targets for inventory, payables and receivables, he said.

Compaq posted gross margins of 24.4 percent in the fourth quarter, at the high-end range of a 22 percent to 24 percent internal target for profitability, Mason said. The company will continue to push for margins in that range but sees efficiency gains offset somewhat by aggressive pricing, he said.
Mason said he is comfortable with analysts' consensus estimates of $1.24 a share earnings for the first quarter 1997 and $5.74 a share earnings for the year.

Compaq posted $462 million or $1.64 a share net income in the fourth quarter, besting analysts' consensus estimate of $1.53 a share for the quarter. Worldwide sales grew 15 percent to $5.4 billion compared with $4.7 billion in the same period last year.
